messages:
maria: heads-up — onboarding customer reported sudden 429s for small-tier plans in APAC this morning after we pushed the new rate-slope policy to canary. stack trace they provided shows quick retries and a bunch of short lived 429s. anyone on call? :thinking:
ravi: on it. which policy did we roll to canary? rp-78a or rp-78b? I saw two variants in the push.
maria: it was rp-78a (slope bump + burst window tweak). 10:12am rollout to apac-canary-1. customer got 429s at 10:23.
lee: pulling logs from rate-proxy now. curious if token buckets are under-provisioned or if we clipped the header parsing. grabbing request headers from the error trace.
lee: quick snippet from logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:23:18Z ERROR request_id=abc123 client=acct-small tier=small policy=rp-78a token_remain=0 bucket_ts=1700000000
2026-03-15T10:23:19Z INFO client=acct-small retry=1 forwarded_to=regional-edge-apac
```
lee: looks like token_remain hit zero then retries piled up. rate service shows a short interval where refill_rate was incorrectly set to 0.5x instead of 1x for small tier — config templating bug?
ravi: ugh — that templating path was changed in recent patch to support dynamic slopes. possible variable name mismatch. the canary manifest uses slope_multiplier: 0.5 for small by mistake.
maria: customer impact: ~15% of calls got 429s for ~8 minutes, they raised a P1. They want rollback.
taylor: billing here — confirm if any billing/overage protections were affected? small-tier customers should not be auto-billed for retries. we might need to freeze charge windows for the affected 8m.
lee: suggest immediate rollback of rp-78a in apac-canary-1 and then patch templating. we can do a scoped rollback (policy only in that canary region) — no global rollback.
ravi: agreed. planning steps: 1) rollback policy in apac-canary-1 2) patch templating var to use slope_multiplier_small: 1.0 3) re-run canary with monitored threshold.
maria: can someone run the rollback now? customer is on the line.
deploy-bot: Authorization required: rbac token needed to hit control-plane.
ravi: I'll run but need a quick approval from @lee for emergency rollback. lee — can you ack?
lee: ack. do the rollback and tag me in followup.
ravi: running rollback — hitting control-plane endpoint. command: 
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/v1/policies/rollback \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RBAC_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"policy_id":"rp-78a","scope":"apac-canary-1","to_version":"rp-78a@2026-03-15T10:05:00Z"}'
```
ravi: returning 202 Accepted from control-plane. rollback job id job-5521. monitoring logs.
lee: saw the rollout stop and previous policy restored at 10:31:12Z. starting to re-ingest token-bucket metrics.
maria: customer reports errors dropped to near zero within 45s after rollback. they are relieved but asking for RCA and credits.
taylor: note for billing: flag affected accounts for 8m window and add credit equal to failed calls estimate. I'll file the billing task after we confirm exact counts.
ravi: root cause: templating variable mismatch introduced in slope feature branch. mitigation: revert canary and patch config. post-fix we'll add a unit test to validate slope variable presence + a dry-run check in manifest pipeline.
lee: also adding an alert to detect refill_rate < 0.8x of expected for any tier during canary pushes. that would have caught this.
maria: next steps: 1) notify customer with timeline & credits 2) schedule postmortem with eng-platform + support + billing 3) re-run canary after tests on staging. I'm drafting message to customer now.
deploy-bot: job job-5521 completed: rollback success.
lee: thanks everyone. I'll own the postmortem doc and link it into the incident tracker.
maria: thanks team — great quick coordination :thumbsup:
taylor: I'll queue billing adjustments and share PR id when ready.
ravi: after we patch, I'll re-run a limited canary with stricter SLIs and manual gate. tagging @lee for gate approval.
maria: closing here unless any objections. moving to incident channel for the postmortem writeup.
lee: no objections. closing thread.
